title: task list --across-refs caches per ref by .quest tree hash so an unchanged ref is never re-read (ODOC-610 / DEC-282 (a1) item 5)
description:
CARRIER from ODOC-610 / DEC-282 item 5, RE-SCOPED to a build by DEC-282 (a1) on 2026-11-19. Read BY REF from opum-doc origin/dev 68734a01 (.quest/planning.json, decision DEC-282, outcomes and (a1)).

Original filing, 2026-11-18, verbatim: "quest-cli: profile task list --across-refs at about 2000 tasks and report before changing anything. Lower priority." The measurement was then the deliverable.

(a1) moved item 5 from "profile first" to build, verbatim: "5. (revised) `task list --across-refs` caches its result per ref, keyed by each ref's .quest tree hash, so an unchanged ref is never re-read. A repeat call with no ref changed answers from the cache, quickly. Proof: wall time and process count at about 2,000 tasks and 40 refs, before and after, plus a test that a second call with unchanged refs reads nothing."

The live case behind it, verbatim from (a1): "A live case on mbam5 at 02:24Z: the Mac's load was 41, with 4-9 concurrent `quest task list --across-refs --allow-partial --json` processes each running 60-90 s ... The repository has 2,313 tasks and 47 worktrees of one clone."

Ships with DEC-282 items 1-4, 7 and 8 in the next lore/quest pair release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: task list --across-refs caches its result per ref, keyed by each ref's .quest tree hash, so an unchanged ref is never re-read
A repeat call with no ref changed answers from the cache without reading any ref
Wall time and process count are measured at about 2,000 tasks and 40 refs, before and after the change, and recorded on this task
A test shows that a second call with unchanged refs reads nothing
bun run check exits 0 with the new test included

implementationNotes: RE-SCOPED 2026-11-19 by DEC-282 (a1), read by ref at opum-doc origin/dev 68734a01: item 5 moved from 'profile first' to build. The old AC1 (profile at about 2000 tasks and report before changing anything) and AC2 (no change before that report) are superseded by the build ACs now on the record; the old scope measured, this one caches per ref keyed by the .quest tree hash and proves it with before/after wall time and process counts plus a no-read second call. Original filing text is kept in the description rather than rewritten.

#763 round 1: REQUEST_CHANGES at c342583873ccf575a982e403a92ea047edf502f8 from the Opus unit quest-cli-review-763, model claude-opus-5-5 (verified by the leader), review worktree review-563-c342583. Leader round-2 scope (one pass): F1 record cold and warm wall time and process count before and after at about 2,000 tasks and 40 refs with the population, fixture counts and cache dir size; F2 prune to the newest 64 by mtime, touch on hit, unlink the temp file on a failed write; F3 remove the unwired whole-result functions and their two tests (they return with QCLI-568 wiring with sha and a request fingerprint in the key); F4 cache the raw location/path/text material keyed by tree hash and re-run the filter, parse, taskState and duplicate check on every read (fingerprint-of-bytes minimum only if the preferred fix costs more than about an hour); F5-F9 all; F10 only if warm wall time at 40 refs is over 5 s. Round 2 is in progress on the same branch. Verdict, byte-verbatim between the relay markers:

VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES at c342583873ccf575a982e403a92ea047edf502f8

Reviewer: read-only. I read the PR diff, `across-refs.ts`, `across-refs-cache.ts`, `local-git.ts`, `ports/git.ts`, the new test file and `.quest/tasks/QCLI-563.json`, all at the head SHA above. I had no shell, so none of the numbers below were measured by me. The process and wall-time figures are your claims or my reading of the code, and I label which.

Overall: the per-ref cache keyed by the `.quest` tree hash is sound, and an unreadable ref is never cached, which is correct. Two things block: the measurement is not on the task record, and the cache can grow without limit.

F1 BLOCKING. AC3 is unmet at this head (`.quest/tasks/QCLI-563.json`)
- The record is still `To Do`. Its only implementation note is the 2026-11-19 re-scope, and no before/after measurement is recorded.
- Your claims also have a gap. You give the cold wall time (86.8 s vs 88.7 s) and the warm process count (2,204 → 125), but not the warm wall time. The ruling's "answers from the cache, quickly" is exactly that number.
- Fix: on this branch, record cold and warm wall time and process count, before and after, at about 2,000 tasks and 40 refs. Name the population used (`--ref` ×40 or open-prs) and the tasks/refs count of the fixture. Also record the size of `across-refs-cache/` after the warm run (F2 needs it).

F2 BLOCKING. The cache has no bound and nothing prunes it (`across-refs-cache.ts:178-191`, `writeJsonAtomically`; `AcrossRefsCache.write` at :239)
- Each distinct `.quest` tree hash ever seen gets a full JSON copy of that ref's whole parsed record set. In the live clone that is about 2,300 records per entry, I estimate several MB each (unmeasured).
- `.quest` changes on nearly every tracker commit on `dev` and on most PR heads, so a new entry lands with almost every tracker change seen by any of the clone's worktrees.
- Nothing deletes entries, `git gc` never touches the directory, and it is invisible to users.
- Fix (cheap): on write, prune to the newest K entries by mtime (for example 64), or by age, and touch an entry on a cache hit so mtime means last used.
- Fix (optional, larger): a two-level content-addressed layout. Store tree hash → `[(path, blobOid)]` manifests plus per-blob records, so consecutive `dev` trees share almost all their storage.
- In the same function: if `writeFile` fails part-way (ENOSPC, for example), the temp file is never unlinked. Add `await unlink(temporary).catch(() => {})` in the catch.

F3 SHOULD. The exported whole-result cache can serve a stale sha, and nothing calls it yet (`across-refs-cache.ts:261-344`, `readAcrossRefsCache`/`writeAcrossRefsCache`)
- Its key is ref NAME → per-ref key (the `.quest` tree hash) only.
- The cached result embeds `refProvenance.sha`, `coverage.refsRead[].sha`, `pullRequest` labels and `discoveredAt`.
- So a PR head that moves without touching `.quest` (most commits) would be served the OLD sha in provenance. The docblock caveat names filter and `--allow-partial` but not this.
- Read validation is also shallow: it does not re-validate the entries.
- Nothing in this PR calls these functions, so this is a trap for QCLI-568, not a live bug.
- Fix: remove both functions and their two tests from this PR so they land with QCLI-568's lock. Or, if they stay, fold the planned sha per ref plus a request fingerprint (filter, `--allow-partial`, population) into the key now. Also update the module docblock's "TWO layers" description, since only layer 1 is wired.

F4 SHOULD. A cache written by one quest build is served to another (`across-refs-cache.ts:101` `CACHE_VERSION`, `:229`)
- The cache lives in the common dir, so every worktree's quest build shares it. In this fleet the installed PATH binary and `bun src/cli/main.ts` run side by side in one clone.
- `taskSchema` is a plain `z.object` (`tasks.ts:394`), which STRIPS unknown keys. So build A writes records already reduced to A's schema.
- Re-running `taskState` on read catches a newer build that is stricter. It does not catch a field that A stripped and B reads or filters on. It also does not catch a change to `CONTINUITY_TASK_LOCATIONS` or to the dot-file filter.
- The only guard is a hand-bumped `CACHE_VERSION`.
- Fix (preferred): cache the RAW material instead of parsed `TaskState`, as `{location: [{path, text}]}` keyed by tree hash. Re-run the dot-file filter, `JSON.parse`, `taskState` and the duplicate-id check on every read, and treat a location missing from the entry as a miss. Parsing is cheap next to the process spawns. After that, `CACHE_VERSION` only describes the document shape.
- Fix (minimum): put a build fingerprint in the directory name. The package version alone is not enough, because one version string can name two byte-sets here.

F5 SHOULD. The "never writes" claims are now false
- `across-refs.ts:46` says "THE VIEW NEVER WRITES".
- `main.ts:493` says "Nothing was written -- the view is read-only".
- On that drift path, every ref that DID read has already been written to the cache.
- Fix: scope the promise to refs, tracker records and the working tree, and name the cache under `<git-common-dir>/quest/across-refs-cache/`. Check that the help text at `command-help.ts:190` ("read-only view") still reads true; I would add one clause naming the cache.

F6 SHOULD. Round-trip fidelity is untested on realistic records (`test/qcli563-across-refs-cache.test.ts`, fixture `taskRecord` at about :88)
- Fixture records have no `createdAt`, no gates or `gateEvents`, and empty checklists.
- A cached record goes through `taskState` twice: once on write and again on read (`normalizeCheckList`, gate replay).
- `identity` (task/collision/unresolved) depends on `createdAt`, which the fixtures never set.
- Fix: add one record with `createdAt`, a gate plus its `gateEvents`, and non-empty acceptance criteria. Assert that warm-call entries deep-equal cold-call entries, including `identity`.

F7 NIT. The "changed ref" test does not assert the new content (test, "a changed ref re-reads ONLY that ref")
- It proves the moved `dev` was re-read but not that the answer reflects the edit.
- Fix: assert that T-1's title is "edited on dev".

F8 NIT. The tests depend on order
- That same test commits onto the shared fixture's `dev`.
- The earlier test's premise `dev:.quest == copy:.quest` holds only because it runs first. `fixture.devSha` is stale afterwards.
- Fix: give the mutating test its own branch or fixture.

F9 NIT. No test covers corruption that parses as valid JSON
- The corrupt-entry test writes non-JSON, so the `taskState` re-validation at `across-refs-cache.ts:229` is not exercised.
- Fix: add a well-formed document whose record fails `taskState`, and assert it falls back to a fresh read.

F10 ADVISORY (d). Where the ~125 warm processes likely go (my reading of the code, not measured)
- About three per ref: `resolveLocal` (`rev-parse`) in planning, `hasRevision` (`cat-file -e`), and `treeHash` (`rev-parse <sha>:.quest`).
- Plus a few fixed calls: origin, `commonDirectory`, and `ls-remote`/`gh` for open-prs.
- Cheap win: one `git cat-file --batch-check` fed `<sha>^{commit}` and `<sha>:.quest` lines for every planned ref answers presence and tree oid in one process. Explicit refs can likewise resolve in one multi-arg `rev-parse`. That takes a warm call to under 10 processes.
- Not blocking unless the warm wall time from F1 says "quickly" is unmet.

Checked and sound
- (a) per-ref key:
  - Records are read only under `.quest/<location>`, so the `.quest` tree hash covers them.
  - Ref name, PR label and sha are re-supplied from the plan on every call.
  - Filters, `--include-archived` and lifecycle policy are applied in `buildEntries` after the cache, so they need no key.
  - `--allow-partial` changes only planning.
  - The `root-<tree>` fallback is content-addressed and correct.
  - The only stale paths are F3 (unwired) and F4.
- (b) concurrency: writes go to a unique temp file and `rename` into place in the same directory, so a reader never sees a torn file. Concurrent writers of one key write equivalent content, and the last one wins harmlessly (the exception is F4's mixed builds). Location `<git-common-dir>/quest/across-refs-cache/` is right. Nothing that lists `<common>/quest/` would trip on the new subdirectory: `id-allocation.ts:637` lists the worktree's `.quest`, not the common dir. Bound: none, see F2.
- (c) the no-read test proves it through a seam that counts `listFilesRequired` and `readBlob` on a FRESH service, so the answer must come from disk. Mutants that turn it red: make `AcrossRefsCache.read` return null, or delete `await cache.write(...)` at `across-refs.ts:779`. A key by sha or by ref name is caught by the "two shas, one read" and "changed ref" tests.
- (e) failure modes: every read and write swallows its own errors. `resolveCache` falls back to null, which disables caching without failing. `acrossRefsRefKey` falls back to undefined, which means read without caching. A corrupt entry is a miss. Unreadable refs bypass the write.
- (f) envelope and exit codes: `main.ts` is untouched by the diff, the envelope shape is the same, and `discoveredAt` is stamped fresh on every call. The writer's "envelope unchanged" claim holds by reading the code.

ACs
- AC1 (per-ref cache keyed by the `.quest` tree hash): MET, subject to F2 and F4.
- AC2 (repeat call answers from the cache without reading any ref): MET as "reads no record". `hasRevision` and `treeHash` still run once per ref. That is unavoidable for a content-addressed key, but the record should say "no record read" rather than "nothing read".
- AC3 (wall time and process count before and after, on the task): NOT MET, see F1.
- AC4 (a test shows a second call reads nothing): MET, scored as "reads no record". The test is mutant-sensitive per (c).
- AC5 (`bun run check` exits 0): NOT VERIFIED by me (no shell). It is plausible, since the only other GitPort stand-ins in tests are `as unknown as GitPort` casts that the two new port methods do not break. Cite the CI `source-gates` run on this head.

#763 round 2: REQUEST_CHANGES at 45aa3bd70630ef2b6cd8ed4033589c2a9d6c32ae from the Opus unit quest-cli-review-763r2, model claude-opus-5-5 (verified by the leader), review worktree review-763-45aa3bd. The PR head has since moved by one fast-forward commit, 52731e451d9d59e9acf38c9a91e0fca1555824be (the main.ts drift hint now names the cache; R2-10 done). Erratum from the unit, supplied by the leader: in section (c), "(R2-4… see R2-4 below, renumbered as R2-4)" should read "(see R2-4)". Leader ruling for round 3: take R2-1 (measure warm at about 2,000 records per ref and add a per-process in-memory materialized cache), R2-2 (preferred fix), R2-3, R2-4, R2-5, R2-10; take the R2-6 to R2-9 nits. The only blocker is F1: the measurement must be ON this task. Round 2 measurement as reported by the specialist (to be superseded by the round-3 table at the live shape): population explicit --ref x40 (refs/heads/ref-1..40), fixture 40 refs x 50 task records = 2,000 task files; before = origin/dev b7db8857 (git archive); this branch is based on 1cce24f1 for the PR history. Cold 14.671 s / 2,204 git processes (dev) vs 14.687 s / 2,166 (branch); warm repeat 15.410 s / 2,204 (dev) vs 0.453 s / 46 (branch); cache dir after the warm run 40 entries, 701,052 bytes, largest entry 17,637 bytes; data byte-identical (2,000 entries); envelope keys unchanged. Round 1 under heavier load: 86.8 s / 88.7 s cold, warm 6.18 s / 125 processes. Verdict, byte-verbatim between the relay markers:

VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES at 45aa3bd70630ef2b6cd8ed4033589c2a9d6c32ae

Reviewer: read-only, with no shell. I read the round-1 verdict, the incremental and full diffs, and these files at the head above: `across-refs-cache.ts`, `across-refs.ts`, `ports/git.ts`, `local-git.ts`, `composition.ts`, the test file and `.quest/tasks/QCLI-563.json`.
- No timing or process count below was measured by me.
- The only blocker is F1: the measurement is not on the record at this head. Everything else is SHOULD or NIT.

## Round-1 findings

| # | State | Evidence at this head |
|---|---|---|
| F1 BLOCKING | **OPEN** | `.quest/tasks/QCLI-563.json` still has `"status":"To Do"`. `implementationNotes` holds exactly ONE entry, the 2026-11-19 re-scope. I matched the whole array as one `"RE-SCOPED…"` string closed by `],"comments"`. None of 0.453 / 2,166 / 2,204 / 701,052 appears in any `.quest/` file, and the full diff touches no `.quest/` path. So the population (`--ref` ×40), the fixture (40 × 50) and the before ref (`b7db8857`) are named only in your claims, not on the task. Fix: commit the note to THIS branch, or cite the ref and SHA where it lives (tracker writes may be confined to the primary checkout). Name both bases: the before is `b7db8857`, but this branch sits on `1cce24f1`. See R2-1 on fixture shape. |
| F2 | **CLOSED** | Write then prune: `across-refs-cache.ts:261-265`. Prune newest-N by mtime: `:278-300`. Touch on hit: `:268-274`, called at `across-refs.ts:854`. Temp file unlinked on failure: `across-refs-cache.ts:314-316`. Tests at `test:660`, `:690`, `:704`. Residuals: R2-4, R2-8, R2-9. |
| F3 | **CLOSED** | `readAcrossRefsCache`/`writeAcrossRefsCache` and their two tests are gone. The docblock (`across-refs-cache.ts:15-51`) now describes one layer. But two tests outside F3's scope went with them (R2-5). |

A missing location is a miss (`:343`), and a non-`records` result falls through to a fresh read (`:860-861`). Residual: the write side pre-filters (R2-2). |
| F5 | **PARTLY CLOSED** | The docblock (`across-refs.ts:47-58`) and the help text (`command-help.ts` across-refs summary, last sentence) are fixed. The `main.ts` hint is pending per your ruling. Its new comment at `main.ts:491-496` must go with it (R2-10). |
| F6 | **CLOSED in substance; the test is weak** | Raw caching removes the double-`taskState` risk by construction. `warm toEqual cold` on a gated record with `createdAt` is at `test:385`. But the identity assertion cannot fail (R2-7). |
| F7 | **CLOSED** | `test:337`: `T-1.title === "edited on dev"`. |
| F8 | **CLOSED** | The mutating test uses its own `mkdtemp` repo. Every shared-fixture test calls `clearCache` first. |
| F9 | **CLOSED** | `test:436`: a well-formed document whose `{id:"T-3"}` fails `taskState` falls back to a fresh read, and the asserted title proves it. |
| F10 | **TAKEN** | `batchCheck` at `local-git.ts:163-185`, used by `probePlannedRefs` at `across-refs.ts:443-490`. Findings: R2-3, R2-6. |

## Checks (b)-(f)

**(b) Can raw caching still serve a stale or wrong answer?** Not stale. The key covers everything read (`.quest/<location>` blobs under that tree). Provenance, filters and lifecycle policy are applied after the cache. Every domain rule is re-run on read except one: the filter also runs BEFORE storage (R2-2).

**(c) batchCheck.**
- Injection: none is possible today. Only 40-hex SHAs reach stdin, because of the filter at `across-refs.ts:452-453`, and specs are `<sha>^{commit}`, `<sha>:.quest` and `<sha>^{tree}`. A ref name with a space or newline never enters the batch.
- Parsing: `missing` is handled, and exit ≠ 0 or a short answer gives an empty map, which falls back per ref. Ambiguity cannot happen with full SHAs.
- The `.quest` answer's object type is not checked, but neither was `rev-parse --verify` before, so this is not a regression.
- Defects: R2-3 (an unparseable line is reported as "missing") and R2-6 (hardening).
- Fallback coverage: an empty map, a thrown error, or a present commit with no key all degrade safely. One real gap: a stale "absent" answer (R2-4… see R2-4 below, renumbered as R2-4).

**(d) Concurrency: sound.**
- An entry unlinked before `readFile` opens it gives ENOENT, which is a miss (`:230-235`).
- One unlinked after open keeps reading on POSIX.
- `touch` on a vanished entry or a read-only filesystem is caught (`:271-273`). On a read-only filesystem, `mkdir`/`writeFile` fail, the write returns false and prune does not run.
- Prune's own unlink races are caught (`:299`).
- In-flight temp files (`.json.<pid>…tmp`) are never counted as entries (`:287`).
- On Windows a rename over an open file can fail; that is caught and simply loses the write.

**(e) Mutant tests.** The diff does not name the five mutants, so I cannot verify "all matched". By reading, these tests turn red under their obvious mutant:
- F9 (`taskState` skipped on read)
- missing location (missing treated as empty)
- dot-file (filter not re-run on read gives malformed, then a fresh read, then non-empty `lastCalls`)
- prune
- touch (no-op)
- failed write (no unlink; only the `unlinked` assertion bites)

The F6 identity assertion is vacuous (R2-7). Two guards have lost their only tests (R2-5). Please list the five mutants and the test each turned red, on the record.

**(f) GitPort.**
- `LocalGitPort` is the only implementer, and `createGitPort` returns it directly (`composition.ts:113-115`).
- Test stand-ins are `as unknown as GitPort` casts (`qcli526:34`, `qcli495:56,297`, `qcli522:234`). Any that reached `probePlannedRefs` without `batchCheck` would throw a TypeError, which is caught at `across-refs.ts:463-467` and falls back per ref. No break.

## New findings

**R2-1 SHOULD (attach to F1). The fixture shape cannot test "quickly" under the F4 design.**
- The fixture is 40 refs × 50 records. A real ~2,000-task repository has every ref carrying the whole tracker; the live case is 2,313.
- After F4, warm cost is no longer process spawns. It is per-record CPU: `materialize` runs `JSON.parse` + zod `taskState` for every record of every ref on every warm call.
- That includes in-memory hits for refs that share a tree: `rawCache` dedups the disk read but not `materialize` (`across-refs.ts:846-858`).
- At live shape that is about 40 × 2,300 ≈ 92k validations per warm call. The 0.453 s figure, taken at 50 per ref, cannot show this.
- Fix:
  1. Measure warm (and record entry size) at about 2,000 records per ref, or state on the record which reading of "about 2,000 tasks" was used and why.
  2. Cache the materialized `records` per `treeKey` in memory for the process. This is safe because it stays within one build, so it does not reopen F4.

**R2-2 SHOULD. The cache is not raw: the writer filters before storing** (`across-refs.ts:898-899`, then `:907`).
- On read, `materialize` can only DROP files, never restore ones the writer skipped.
- A build with a wider filter (or one that reads a currently skipped name) is therefore silently served a SHORTER record set. That is a wrong answer, not a miss.
- The docblock at `across-refs-cache.ts:30-36` ("never hand another build a record it would not itself produce") is true only for additions. The dot-file test (`test:474`) covers only the stricter-reader direction.
- Fix (preferred): store every path from `listFilesRequired` per location, with `text: null` for paths the writer did not read. On read, treat it as a miss if the current filter selects a path whose text is null.
- Fix (minimum): state in `CACHE_VERSION`'s docblock that a filter change requires a bump, and narrow the module docblock's claim.

**R2-3 SHOULD. `batchCheck` reports an unrecognised line as "missing"** (`local-git.ts:181-182`).
- `/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/` failing sets `null`, which means "missing". The caller reads that as `present: false`, so a `--ref` with no `sourceRef` goes straight to "not present in this repository" (`across-refs.ts:820-823`).
- The port contract (`ports/git.ts:82-84`) says an unanswerable spec must be ABSENT from the map so the caller falls back.
- Fix: map only `<spec> missing` to null. Leave `ambiguous` and any unparseable line out of the map.
- Better still, confirm alignment by checking that a missing line equals exactly `` `${spec} missing` ``, and return an empty map if any does not.

**R2-4 SHOULD. A stale "absent" probe forces a needless fetch, and that fetch can fail** (`across-refs.ts:815-835`).
- The batch runs once before the sequential loop. Suppose a sha absent at probe time becomes present before its turn: either two planned refs share the sha, or an earlier PR fetch brought it in as an ancestor.
- That ref still goes down the fetch path. The old per-ref `hasRevision` found it present and did not fetch.
- Offline or on a transient failure, this marks a ref unreadable whose object is local: a false incomplete coverage.
- Fix: when `probe.present === false`, re-run `hasRevision` before fetching. That path is cold-only and rare, so the extra spawn is noise.

**R2-5 SHOULD. Two tests outside F3's scope were deleted, and two guards are now untested.**
- "AcrossRefsCache ignores a document written for a different key" covered `document.key !== key` (`across-refs-cache.ts:241`) and the `KEY_PATTERN` path-traversal miss (`:229`, `"../../escape"`). Deleting either guard now keeps 14/14 green.
- The CLI composition test (exit 0, empty stderr, cache dir created through `main.ts`) is also gone. That is NIT, since `viewWith` exercises the default `resolveCache`.
- Fix: restore the first test, adapted to `locations`.

**R2-6 NIT. `batchCheck` hardening** (`local-git.ts:173-174`):
- use `lines.length !== specs.length`, not `<`;
- return an empty map if any spec contains `\n` or `\r`, so a future caller passing names cannot desync the alignment. The port accepts arbitrary specs.

**R2-7 NIT. The F6 identity assertion cannot fail** (`test:385-424`).
- The view is a single ref, and `identityOf` returns `task` for fewer than 2 states (`across-refs.ts:279`).
- `AcrossRefsEntry` and `AcrossRefsState` (`:77-80`, `:117-133`) carry no `createdAt` or gate field, so the deep-equal cannot see them either.
- Fix: run over `["refs/heads/dev","refs/heads/feature"]` and assert T-10 is `task` (shared `createdAt`) and T-1 is `unresolved` (none), warm equal to cold.

**R2-8 NIT, rising to SHOULD above 64 open PRs. Prune thrashes when one run uses more than `maxEntries` keys** (`across-refs-cache.ts:265`, `:296-299`).
- Prune runs after every write. A run with more than 64 distinct trees evicts its own early entries, and the next identical run then misses every one of them: the LRU sequential-scan pattern, with a hit rate near 0.
- It is harmless at 40.
- Fix: prune once at the end of `view()` with this run's keys exempt, or bound by `max(64, 2 × planned refs)`.
- Related: the bound counts entries, not bytes. At live shape (R2-1), measure one entry before settling on 64.

**R2-9 NIT.**
- A writer killed between `writeFile` and `rename` leaves a `.tmp` that prune never reclaims (`:287`). Fix: also unlink `.tmp` files older than about 1 h.
- In the failed-write test (`test:704`), the "no `.tmp` in files" assertion is vacuous because the stub throws before storing anything. Add a case where `rename` fails after `writeFile` succeeded, which is where residue actually occurs.

**R2-10 NIT (known pending).** The comment at `main.ts:491-496` says the hint wording is "DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED" and must be routed to opum-cli-e2e. That contradicts your ruling, so delete it when the hint changes.

## ACs

| AC | Status |
|---|---|
| AC1 | MET |
| AC2 | MET, as "no record read" |
| AC3 | **NOT MET** (F1) |

- The live population is open PRs into dev. Most PR heads touch `.quest`, or sit on a different dev commit, so they have DISTINCT trees of full size. There the memory cache does nothing, and each warm call reads and parses about 40 full documents and runs `taskState` on about 80k records. That per-record CPU is exactly what R2-1 named, and it is unmeasured.

- Synthetic records average about 348 B (695,709 / 2,000). Real records are far larger: QCLI-563.json alone is tens of KB. So "64 entries ≈ 45 MB" is a floor, not a bound. At realistic sizes, 41 protected entries per run plus 64 others could reach hundreds of MB inside .git.

## (a7)/(a8)
Nothing here makes the Q568-INT join harder, provided whole-result entries live in their own directory. In this one, prune would evict them (they are never in `usedKeys`), and `read` rejects any key that is not KEY_PATTERN.

Concurrent unlocked runs, which (a8) allows on expiry, are safe:
- Writes are a unique temp file plus rename.
- Different-filter builds can only ping-pong an entry between a miss and a rewrite, never serve a wrong set.
- A concurrent prune can only cost performance.

One undetermined point to route, not block on: the cache swallows an unwritable directory or ENOSPC silently, so every run quietly falls back to the cold path. That is the "silent storm" (a8) item 2 rejected for the lock. Its text binds the lock, not this cache.
